headline: Eight Artisans from Eight States Showcase India’s Craftsmanship
fullText:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises

PM Vishwakarma Artisans Showcase India’s Traditional Crafts at BRICS Cultural Bazar

Traditional craftsmanship takes centre stage at the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at Parliament House Complex, New Delhi

27 OCT 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi

Artisans and craftspeople under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises participated at the two-day Cultural Bazar organised during the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at the Parliament House Complex, New Delhi, on 26–27 October 2026.

The Cultural Bazar provided a platform to showcase India’s rich cultural heritage, traditional crafts, artisan-made products and indigenous skills to national and international delegates attending the BRICS Parliamentary Forum.

The participation highlighted the diversity of India’s traditional craftsmanship and the contribution of artisan communities to preserving the country’s cultural legacy. BRICS delegates also appreciated the products made by Vishwakarmas.

Eight Artisans from Eight States Showcase India’s Craftsmanship

Eight PM Vishwakarma artisans and craftspeople from Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Nagaland, Karnataka and Maharashtra participated in the Cultural Bazar, showcasing India’s diverse traditional craftsmanship.

Representing traditional trades such as Tailor, Goldsmith, Sculptor/Stone Carver, Doll and Toy Maker, and Cobbler, the artisans displayed their handcrafted products at the PM Vishwakarma stall. Selected artisans also conducted live demonstrations of traditional craft-making techniques, offering visitors an opportunity to witness the skills and craftsmanship involved in creating these products.

The participation provided a valuable platform to enhance the visibility and recognition of traditional artisans, expand market exposure and highlight the impact of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme in preserving traditional skills and empowering artisan communities.

1. Makbul Jadu Patiya | Jharkhand | Dokra Artisan

Makbul Jadu Patiya showcases the traditional Dokra metal craft, known for its intricate designs and the ancient lost-wax casting technique. Through the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, he participated in exhibitions, including Dilli Haat and the State Trade Fair, gaining wider market exposure. His onboarding on Amazon has further opened opportunities to expand his customer base and strengthen his livelihood.

2. Anurag Sahu | Madhya Pradesh | Stone Sculptor

Anurag Sahu specialises in hand-carved marble statues, pooja articles, souvenirs and home décor products made from New Bhedaghat Marble of Jabalpur. Practising the GI-tagged Jabalpur Stone Craft, he combines traditional artistry with intricate detailing. With support under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, he has been onboarded on Amazon and Flipkart, helping him take his products online and expand his business.

3. Bajirao Shamrao Satpute | Maharashtra | Cobbler

Bajirao Shamrao Satpute preserves the traditional leather craftsmanship of Kolhapur through handcrafted Kolhapuri chappals, featuring intricate detailing and the distinctive Nach Mauri Patta design. Through the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, he participated in a state-level exhibition and was onboarded on Amazon, gaining opportunities for better product branding, wider market reach and greater social recognition while preserving traditional craftsmanship.

4. Deepu S | Karnataka | Doll and Toy Maker

Deepu S specialises in traditional Channapatna toys and Kinhal toys, reflecting Karnataka’s rich toy-making heritage. Under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, he received a toolkit, completed skill training and was onboarded on the Meesho e-commerce platform, creating opportunities to showcase his traditional products to a wider customer base.

5. Dheeraj Kumar | Bihar | Stone Sculptor

Dheeraj Kumar creates intricate wooden and stone sculptures of Lord Buddha and other deities, reflecting Gaya’s deep historical connection with Buddhism. His handcrafted creations are supplied to Bodh Gaya and other districts across Bihar. Under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, loan assistance helped him purchase raw materials, while the toolkit improved his ability to cut, grind and polish his creations with better finishing.

6. Mohamad Nasim | Rajasthan | Goldsmith

Mohamad Nasim creates traditional lac bangles adorned with vibrant colours, decorative stones and intricate handcrafted designs, showcasing Rajasthan’s rich jewellery-making heritage. Through the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, he received skill training, a modern toolkit and loan assistance, and was onboarded on Amazon. This support has helped him enhance his craftsmanship, expand his business and increase his income.

7. Masrat Fayaz | Jammu and Kashmir | Tailor

Masrat Fayaz specialises in tailoring shawls, stoles, traditional Kashmiri pherans and Pashmina shawls. Through the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, she enhanced her tailoring skills and gained access to modern tools, improving product quality, finishing and productivity. Her participation in prestigious government exhibitions has helped her showcase her creations and explore wider market opportunities while preserving Kashmir’s traditional textile heritage.

8. Throngli Sangtam | Nagaland | Doll and Toy Maker

Throngli Sangtam creates handmade crochet dolls inspired by traditional Naga attire, tribal motifs and cultural symbols, bringing Nagaland’s heritage to life through yarn craftsmanship. With over 100 dolls in stock, she has participated in Dilli Haat and is associated with the collective Mother’s Craft. Loan assistance helped her invest in quality raw materials, while an MoU with the Department of Women Resource Development has opened opportunities to sell her products through the MyKi store.

### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises’ PM Vishwakarma artisans showcased India’s traditional crafts at the BRICS Cultural Bazar during the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at the Parliament House Complex, New Delhi, on 26–27 October 2026, highlighting the scheme’s role in preserving artisan heritage and expanding market access.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Event Details**: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum; two‑day Cultural Bazar; 26–27 October 2026; venue – Parliament House Complex, New Delhi; organized by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme.  
- **Artisan Participation**: Eight artisans from eight states (Rajasthan, Jammu & Kashmir, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Nagaland, Karnataka, Maharashtra) demonstrated traditional crafts.  
- **Crafts Represented**: Tailor, Goldsmith, Sculptor/Stone Carver, Doll and Toy Maker, Cobbler (including Dokra metalwork, marble carving, leather footwear, Channapatna/Kinhal toys, wooden/stone sculptures, lac bangles, Kashmiri shawl tailoring, crochet dolls).  
- **Individual Profiles & Achievements**:  
  - **Makbul Jadu Patiya** (Jharkhand – Dokra Artisan): Exhibited at Dilli Haat and State Trade Fair; onboarded on Amazon.  
  - **Anurag Sahu** (Madhya Pradesh – Stone Sculptor): Specialises in Jabalpur Marble GI‑tagged craft; onboarded on Amazon and Flipkart.  
  - **Bajirao Shamrao Satpute** (Maharashtra – Cobbler): Showcases Kolhapuri chappals; participated in state‑level exhibition; onboarded on Amazon.  
  - **Deepu S** (Karnataka – Doll and Toy Maker): Received toolkit and training; onboarded on Meesho for Channapatna/Kinhal toys.  
  - **Dheeraj Kumar** (Bihar – Stone Sculptor): Utilised loan assistance for raw materials and toolkit for improved finishing of Buddha and deity sculptures.  
  - **Mohamad Nasim** (Rajasthan – Goldsmith): Received skill training, toolkit, loan; onboarded on Amazon for lac bangles.  
  - **Masrat Fayaz** (Jammu & Kashmir – Tailor): Upgraded tailoring skills and tools; participated in government exhibitions for shawl and pheran products.  
  - **Throngli Sangtam** (Nagaland – Doll and Toy Maker): Produces >100 crochet dolls; involved in Dilli Haat and Mother’s Craft collective; received loan assistance; MoU with Department of Women Resource Development for MyKi store.  
- **Support Under PM Vishwakarma Scheme**: Provision of toolkits, skill training, loan assistance, and e‑commerce platform onboarding (Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, Mother’s Craft, MyKi store) to enhance visibility, market reach, and livelihoods.

headline: 1. Workplace Cleanliness and Facility Improvement
fullText:
Ministry of Textiles

Ministry of Textiles Highlights Significant Achievements of Central Silk Board under Special Campaign 6

27 OCT 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Textiles highlights the significant achievements and dedicated efforts of the Central Silk Board (CSB) under Special Campaign 6, being undertaken with the objective of promoting cleanliness, improving workplace efficiency, reducing pendency, and ensuring the effective management of records and resources across government offices.

The Central Silk Board has actively participated in the campaign by undertaking various activities and initiatives focused on cleanliness, systematic record management, disposal of obsolete materials, and optimum utilization of available office space. These efforts reflect the Board’s commitment to fostering a clean, organized, and efficient working environment.

As part of the campaign, various initiatives have been undertaken to promote cleanliness in office premises, review and streamline physical and electronic records, identify redundant materials for disposal, and ensure the proper management of scrap and e-waste in accordance with applicable guidelines. These activities also aim to strengthen institutional efficiency, enhance accountability, and promote environmentally responsible practices.

Key Activities & Initiatives

1. Workplace Cleanliness and Facility Improvement

Deep-cleaning and upkeep of office rooms, laboratories, workbenches, corridors, storage areas and common facilities are being undertaken across CSB establishments.

A noteworthy initiative is the renovation of office washrooms, recognizing the importance of clean, hygienic and functional sanitation facilities for staff working long hours. Cleaning of campuses, pathways, parking areas, drinking-water points and other common facilities, along with removal of weeds & unwanted vegetation, part of the campaign.

2. Record Management and Space Optimisation

Record rooms and storage racks are being cleaned and reorganized; old files are being reviewed and records identified for weeding are being processed in accordance with applicable retention schedules and rules. Workbenches/work areas are being kept clutter-free, while unused & damaged materials are being identified for removal to improve accessibility, safety and efficient utilization.

3. E-waste and Scrap Management

Obsolete IT and telecommunication equipment, e-waste, scrap and damaged furniture are being segregated and processed for disposal through prescribed procedures. As reported in the campaign progress data, 75 obsolete IT/telecommunication equipment items were identified for disposal, including desktop computers, printers& laptops.

4. Awareness, 4R Practices and Environmental Sustainability

Awareness campaigns, seminars and presentations are being conducted to promote the 4Rs- Refuse, Reduce, Reuse and Recycle and responsible waste management.

Activities under SHS 2026 included cleanliness drives, rallies, tree plantation, waste segregation awareness, home composting and vermicomposting demonstrations, and promotion of eco-friendly practices at farms and campuses.

Safai Mitra Samman Shivir activities included distribution of personal protective equipment (PPE) and felicitation of sanitation workers. Staff health-check-up programmes were also organized as part of the SHS campaign.

5. Social Media Outreach and Publicity

CSB’s official social media platforms, X, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp Channels, as applicable were used to disseminate updates and photographs of activities undertaken by the Board’s Institutes, Offices and Nested Units under and Special Campaign 6. These social media updates helped document campaign activities, strengthen awareness and encourage participation in cleanliness and environmental responsibility.

Through Special Campaign 6 2026 activities, CSB is reinforcing a culture of cleanliness, accountability, environmental responsibility & efficient workplace management. Initiatives such as office washroom renovation, cleaning of laboratories & campuses, clutter-free work areas, systematic record management, e-waste segregation and 4R awareness contribute to a healthier & better-organized work environment. Publicity through CSB’s social media platforms has supported documentation, awareness and wider dissemination of these initiatives across its establishments.

The initiatives undertaken by the Central Silk Board demonstrate its proactive participation in the Government of India’s Special Campaign 6 and its commitment to the principles of Swachhata, good governance, and sustainable resource management. The Ministry of Textiles continues to encourage all its attached and subordinate offices, organizations, and public sector undertakings to actively participate in the campaign and work towards achieving the targets set under Special Campaign 6.

(Release ID: 2328968)
